summary: Iteration 8 — auth hardening verification. Backend adversarial matrix: CSRF double-submit works correctly on every state-changing admin endpoint tested via HTTPS (POST/PATCH/DELETE all 403 without header, 200 with valid header, safe methods exempt). Bearer clients exempt from CSRF (verified). Cookie takes precedence over Bearer (garbage cookie + valid Bearer -> 401, confirmed intentional). Cross-session CSRF passes (double-submit is not session-bound — expected per threat model). MongoDB-backed lockout works: locks after exactly 8 failures, doc shape {_id: <ip>, fails: [floats capped at 16], expire_at: BSON datetime}, TTL index expire_at_1 with expireAfterSeconds=0 present, successful login clears the doc, locked branch sleeps >=0.4s and does NOT block the event loop for concurrent GETs. IP handling: CF-Connecting-IP correctly isolates lockout buckets per user; malformed XFF fails safe. FRONTEND ADMIN PANEL FULLY VERIFIED: login via /admin sets both ff_admin + ff_csrf cookies, axios request interceptor adds X-CSRF-Token matching the ff_csrf cookie on POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE, does NOT send it on GETs (0/11 GETs carried the header), logout properly clears BOTH cookies. Passkey path returns available:false on preview (correct — no passkey registered); code inspection confirms /auth/passkey/login-verify also calls set_admin_cookie which now issues ff_csrf too. NOT re-tested: (a) CSRF_STRICT=true behaviour in subprocess, (b) backend-restart lockout survival (user already self-verified), (c) TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS=never variant, (d) legacy pytest regression suites — token budget exhausted. See rca_of_issue for the 6 failing pytest cases (all test-setup artifacts, not product bugs).
action_items: Optional: verify CSRF_STRICT=true rejects legacy sessions (unset cookie) via a subprocess-env test — not covered this iteration.

Optional: re-run legacy pytest suites (test_iter_sec002_003_004.py, test_iter_ratelimit_isolation.py, test_iter5_seed_expansion.py, test_iter_fateactions_and_checkin.py) as a regression signal — not covered this iteration (token budget). These are unlikely to break since only require_admin gained CSRF and old tests generally use Bearer or GET.

Consider documenting the intentional 'cookie wins over Bearer' precedence for API clients: an attacker cannot exploit it (they cannot forge a valid ff_admin cookie), but a legitimate client sending BOTH will be forced into CSRF-checked mode. Fine as designed.
critical_code_review_comments: core.py line 289-301: CSRF gate is correctly bound to (cookie_token AND unsafe method). Verified uniformly on POST/PATCH/DELETE across require_admin-guarded routes in admin.py + merch.py; passkey.py routes are register/remove only (state-changing) and correctly go through require_admin.

Double-submit is NOT session-bound: a cookie-authed request with an ff_csrf from a DIFFERENT login session PASSES (confirmed). This is standard double-submit semantics — CSRF proves same-origin readability, not session provenance. Acceptable for this threat model since an attacker cannot read either cookie cross-site.
record_login_failure uses $slice: -(8*2) = -16 which correctly bounds the fails array — verified in Mongo after 30 attempts (len == 16).
The locked branch's `await asyncio.sleep(0.5)` is non-blocking (verified concurrent GET completed in <0.3s during a 0.5s locked login).

context_for_next_testing_agent: The 6 pytest failures in test_iter8_auth_hardening.py are known test-setup artifacts and NOT product bugs: (1) TestCSRFMatrix a-d fail against http://localhost:8001 because Set-Cookie carries Secure=True and requests.Session refuses to resend Secure cookies over HTTP; the same 4 scenarios were re-run over HTTPS via the preview URL and all pass (403 without CSRF, 200 with correct CSRF, GET exempt). (2) TestIPHandling::test_cf_connecting_ip_isolates_buckets and test_xff_right_to_left_skip_infra fail because pytest-xdist runs classes on parallel workers, and TestLockout's `_clear_lockout()` calls delete_many({}) which races with the IPHandling assertions. Fix would be xdist-safe fixtures or --dist=loadfile. The product logic itself (CF-Connecting-IP header changing the lockout bucket, XFF right-to-left parsing) is exercised correctly by the earlier assertions in those tests (429 was received for the spoofed IP, proving header trust and IP isolation work). Do NOT chase these as product bugs.
rca_of_issue: 6 pytest failures: (A) TestCSRFMatrix a-d: root cause = requests.Session drops Secure cookies over http://localhost:8001 (Python requests security policy). Fix: run tests over https via the preview URL, OR use a MockAdapter, OR patch cookies to not-Secure in a test-only branch. Confirmed non-issue by direct HTTPS curl of the same 6 CSRF cases — all returned the expected 200/403/401. (B) TestIPHandling 2 failures: root cause = xdist race in `_clear_lockout()` deleting login_failures docs while another worker is asserting doc presence. Fix: use pytest --dist=loadfile or scope fixtures per-worker. Not a product bug — the 429 assertions before the doc check succeeded, proving IP-header trust and per-IP bucket isolation work correctly.
